title: Cutflow & LTS gating: release tooling for weekly build trains
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a repeatable, automated cutflow for weekly build trains that enforces channeled LTS gating and produces deterministic RC tags and release notes. Deliverables include a CLI/CI workflow that performs cut validation, automated RC tagging logic, release notes generation from linked PRs and changelogs, and a minimal upgrade tool to orchestrate customer-facing channel promotions and post-release migrations.
background: Engineering and Platform teams currently perform manual steps to cut weekly builds: tag creation, sanity checks, and collating release notes. This manual process is error-prone during high-velocity weeks and creates variability across hosted, dedicated, and private channels. We need a coded cutflow that integrates gating rules for LTS candidate channels and emits artifacts used by Console and Dedicated rollout systems.
scope: Prototype and land automation for the weekly cut: (1) a CI-native cut pipeline with preflight checks, (2) deterministic RC tagging following semver+channel rules, (3) release-notes automation that aggregates merged PRs and eval regressions, (4) a minimal upgrade promotion tool to push releases between channels (canary -> stable -> LTS). Excludes full UI in Console (follow-up work).
approach: Build a GitHub Actions workflow (also adaptable to our internal CI) to run pre-cut validations: green e2e pipelines, benchmark guardrails (latency regressions < 5%), and permissive test matrix. Implement a tagging module that computes tag names using the pattern v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>-rc.<N>-<channel>. Add a release-notes generator that uses PR labels and the CHANGELOG directory to create a markdown artifact and attach to the release. Provide a CLI to promote tags across channels that call the rollout API and create an automated rollout plan with gates (manual approval + health checks).
versioning_policy: Adopt semver with channel suffixes. Weekly non-breaking additions increment PATCH. Breaking changes bump MINOR. LTS channels receive stabilized MINOR versions; LTS candidates are frozen after RC passes three consecutive stabilization cycles. RC tag format: v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>-rc.<ITER>-<channel> (e.g., v1.20.3-rc.1-ltscandidate). The promotion tooling will strip rc.<ITER> on final release tag.
gating_rules: Pre-cut gates: CI green, perf no-regressions, security-scan passes. Post-cut gates for channel promotion: canary must maintain error-rate < 0.2% and latency SLO for 48h before promoting to stable. LTS promotion requires a 3-week extra monitoring window and sign-off from Product and Support. Auto-rollback if critical SLOs breach during promotion window.
rc_tagging_process: Automation will calculate iteration number by reading existing rc tags for same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and incrementing the highest iteration. RC creation step will: create tag, push tag, create Draft GitHub Release with generated notes, run quick smoke e2e and perf suite, and mark RC as 'validated' or 'needs-attention' based on results.
release_notes_automation: Gather merged PRs since last stable tag using GitHub API; prioritize PRs with labels: feature, bug, security, regression. Include eval/regression summary from our nightly eval dashboard (link attached). Format release notes into sections: Highlights, Fixed, Known Issues, Upgrade Notes. Output artifact: markdown + JSON summary used by Console and Release pages.
upgrade_tooling: Small CLI (python/Go) with commands: plan, promote, rollback, status. 'plan' generates affected upgrades for Dedicated/Private customers, including DB migrations and compat warnings. 'promote' triggers API calls to rollout engine with gates and automated checks. 'rollback' attempts safe revert (if supportable) and notifies stakeholders. 'status' surfaces rollouts in-flight. The tool will store audit events in our Release Audit log for compliance.
testing_plan: Unit tests for tagging and release-note parsers
Integration tests exercising CI workflow in a sandbox repo
Performance guard rails run against representative models and synthetic load
Canary promotion simulation that injects lat/err anomalies to verify auto-rollback
Manual end-to-end dry-run with private deployment to validate upgrade CLI

decision_log: 2026-03-03: Chose semver+channel suffix over calendar-based tags to keep interoperability with downstream tooling.
2026-03-05: Agreed to require 48h canary window for stable promotion; LTS promotion requires 3-week stabilization.
2026-03-09: Opted for GitHub Actions prototype with pluggable adapters to internal CI later on.
risks: Automation could introduce silent tag collisions if multiple cut jobs run concurrently — mitigated via repo-level cut lock file
Perf regression guardrails may be flaky across regions; require robust baselining
Private customers with pinned images may need manual coordination for LTS promotions
rollout_schedule: Week 0 (this cycle): land GitHub Action + tagging module behind feature flag
Week 1: enable release-notes generator and publish draft releases automatically
Week 2: pilot promotion CLI for non-customer-facing canary in staging
Week 3: enable canary -> stable auto-promote for internal services, keep manual LTS promotion
Week 4: evaluate and expand to Dedicated and Private channels
open_questions: Do we enforce a max number of RC iterations before blocking? (proposal: 6)
What telemetry threshold values are acceptable for auto-promotion for each channel?
Should release notes include non-public internal-only notes for Support?
